title: AI Learning Design and Knowledge Transfer

questions.question: What is the main weakness of generic AI-generated training text?
options: It can create content volume without role transfer or behavior change
It cannot be produced quickly enough to keep up with enablement demand
It uses vocabulary that most learners in the target role will not recognise
It leaves out the learning objectives that a course outline normally states
questions.explanation: Learning design must target role outcomes and transfer. Generic AI text creates training volume without behavior change.

questions.question: A team asks for "an AI training". What does this lesson say that request usually hides?
options: A budget approval, a room booking, a trainer assignment, or a calendar slot
A tooling request, a licence purchase, an account setup, or an access ticket
A compliance deadline, an audit finding, a policy update, or a mandatory sign-off
A role skill gap, a guided practice format, a job aid, or a knowledge check
questions.explanation: The lesson translates a generic training request into something specific: a role skill gap, a guided practice format, a job aid, or a knowledge check. Design starts from the role outcome, not from the wording of the request.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact recommend?
options: The HR policy that governs how training hours are recorded
The optimizer settings for a model trained on course material
The right learning form and controls for an enablement scenario
The manager decisions that follow once a learner has finished
questions.explanation: The artifact maps learning signals - skill gap, role context, practice need, assessment need - to a learning form and its controls.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: A knowledge check that tests the target behavior, not just recall of the text
An objective written after the course content has already been drafted
A practice task replaced by a longer reading section to save session time
A manager handoff dropped once the learner has completed the material
questions.explanation: Knowledge checks provide evidence that learning happened, and the lesson asks that they test the target behavior. Objective checks, practice tasks, and manager handoff are the other controls.

questions.question: When is a workshop a better fit than a micro lesson?
options: When the topic is broad enough that a single short lesson cannot cover it
When learners need guided practice, discussion, and role-specific transfer
When the material changes often and a live format is cheaper to update
When the audience is large enough to fill a scheduled session properly
questions.explanation: Workshops are useful when guided practice, discussion, and role-specific transfer matter, not simply when a topic is long.

questions.question: What should AI learning design start with?
options: Role outcome, target behavior, practice task, and transfer evidence
A content outline, a slide count, a session length, and a trainer note
A tool list, a vendor demo, an access request, and a licence assignment
A draft article, a summary prompt, a review pass, and a publish decision
questions.explanation: Transfer-focused design keeps AI-generated training useful: define the role, the behavior, the practice task, and the evidence that learning happened before drafting anything.
